title: Removal of orthopedic hardware
what: The surgeon removes the plate, screws, or wires placed for a fracture. Usually through the same cut.
why: When the bone has healed and the metal bothers you, hurts, or is due to come out as planned.
duration: surgery usually takes 30 to 90 minutes; you often go home the same day or the next
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Allergies to medicines, latex, or iodine
When and where the metal was placed. Your discharge papers will help
Heart or lung disease, or diabetes

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, and sometimes a GP checkup. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthetist will talk with you. Tell them about your health and medicines.

prepare.title: Food and water
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: X-rays
prepare.text: A recent X-ray is usually needed before surgery. Check with the clinic.

bring: Discharge papers from the earlier surgery
steps: You change, and an IV line is placed
General or local anesthesia is given, depending on the surgery
The surgeon opens the old scar
The screws are unscrewed, and the plate or rod is removed
The wound is stitched and bandaged
feel: The area hurts for a few days. You will get painkillers
after: Increase activity gradually. The bone at the screw holes takes a few weeks to strengthen
Keep the dressing dry until you are told it is OK
Stitches usually come out after 10 to 14 days
red_flags: A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness and pus from the wound
Sudden pain or a change in shape after putting weight on it: see a doctor right away
Sudden shortness of breath or chest pain: call emergency services

faq.q: Does the metal have to come out?
faq.a: No. It can often stay. You decide together with your surgeon.

faq.q: Can I put weight on the limb right away?
faq.a: Usually yes, carefully, but no jumping or heavy lifting for the first weeks.

reminders.text: Hardware removal tomorrow. Bring the discharge papers from your earlier surgery and your X-rays.
